controls.title: Embedded passwords, API keys, tokens, private URLs in current source
controls.evidence: Gitleaks 8.30.1 working-tree scan: 2 hits, both YouTube's public web-client key and BotGuard request key in PoTokenWebView.kt (public identifiers from YouTube's own web player / upstream NewPipe). 0 after the reviewed allowlist (.gitleaks.toml). Manual grep: no passwords, tokens or keystore values in source.
controls.remediation: Keep the .gitleaks.toml allowlist narrow (file + line pattern).

controls.title: Secrets in Git history
controls.evidence: gitleaks git --log-opts=--all over all 63 commits on every branch: only the same 2 public YouTube identifiers. git log --name-only: keystores, keystore.properties, firebase.properties, cloud.properties, google-services.json and server/.env were never committed.
controls.remediation: None needed. History is not rewritten.

controls.title: .gitignore covers sensitive files
controls.evidence: .gitignore excludes keystore.properties, *.jks, *.keystore, firebase.properties, google-services.json, cloud.properties, server/.env, server/navi-creds.txt, server/navidrome-data, local.properties, dist/, *.apk/*.aab. Added *.p12 / *.pfx.

controls.title: Release keystore and passwords excluded from Git
controls.evidence: Signing key is ~/.android/debug.keystore outside the repo; passwords only in the gitignored keystore.properties; neither ever appears in history (control 2). CI check 'No signing material tracked in git' added.

controls.title: GitHub Actions secret exposure
controls.evidence: Workflows use no secrets; default token read-only (repository setting + 'permissions: contents: read'); checkout uses persist-credentials: false; no pull_request_target; signing and publishing never run in Actions.

controls.title: Credential exposure in docs, screenshots, logs, release assets
controls.evidence: docs/REMOTE_ACCESS.md published the Tailscale tailnet name, MagicDNS host name, account prefix and Tailscale IP. Redacted to placeholders in the current tree. No screenshots are tracked (only icon images). Release assets are APKs, SHA256SUMS.txt and notes from CHANGELOG (no private data). The old values remain in earlier commits of the public repository.
controls.remediation: Fixed in the tree. Owner decision: leave history as is (tailnet addresses are reachable only by your own Tailscale devices) or rewrite public history.

controls.title: Dependency licenses and attribution
controls.evidence: THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md and docs/DEPENDENCIES.md list licenses; BitChord-derived files keep their GPL headers. This change adds no new shipped library (version bumps only). Gitleaks, OSV and CodeQL run only in CI/locally and are not shipped.

controls.title: Documented secret-rotation procedure
controls.evidence: New docs/security/SECRET_ROTATION.md: Navidrome password, Firebase config, GitHub token, party server, YouTube session; the signing key is explicitly NOT rotated without a planned migration.

controls.title: Dangerous / unnecessary permissions
controls.evidence: READ_MEDIA_AUDIO (READ_EXTERNAL_STORAGE up to API 32), FOREGROUND_SERVICE (+MEDIA_PLAYBACK; DATA_SYNC in full), POST_NOTIFICATIONS, INTERNET, ACCESS_NETWORK_STATE, REQUEST_INSTALL_PACKAGES (updater; the user confirms every install), RECEIVE_BOOT_COMPLETED (full: resume downloads), WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE up to API 28. No location, contacts, camera, microphone, SMS or accessibility.

controls.title: Exported activities, services, receivers, providers
controls.evidence: Exported: MainActivity (launcher, invite and share links) and PlaybackService (Media3 session for Bluetooth/Auto/system controls). Both FileProviders are exported=false. Library components are exported only behind system permissions, plus 3 reviewed Firebase/Play-services entries. New scripts/security/check_manifest.py fails on any unreviewed exported component in the merged release manifests; SecurityRegressionTest pins the app's own list.

controls.title: Deep links, intents and PendingIntents
controls.evidence: All PendingIntents are FLAG_IMMUTABLE except the PackageInstaller status callback, which must be mutable and is explicit (component + package; receiver not exported). mimic://party invites only show a card and joining needs a tap; hostile server values are dropped (tests). YouTube/TikTok VIEW filters are never the default handler; shared text must contain a URL.

controls.title: WebView JavaScript, navigation and file access
controls.evidence: PoToken WebView: blockNetworkLoads=true; its JavaScript interface is reachable only by its own local page. YouTube Music sign-in WebView: JavaScript is required by Google sign-in, no JavaScript interface; file and content access now explicitly off. No onReceivedSslError override.

controls.title: Production debugging and development settings
controls.evidence: Release APKs are not debuggable and not testOnly (aapt2 badging, checked by the release gate); the online DebugLog sink is never installed; Log.* lines carry status codes and class names only.

controls.title: Backup and data-extraction policy
controls.evidence: allowBackup=true with empty rules sent everything to Google cloud backup, including the YouTube Music session (EncryptedSharedPreferences, or plain prefs on its fallback path), WebView cookies, the Listen Together token and the Navidrome store. Fixed: backup_rules.xml (Android 6-11) and data_extraction_rules.xml (cloud backup + device transfer, Android 12+) exclude all sign-in stores; settings, library, playlists and themes are still backed up.
controls.remediation: Effect: after restoring onto a NEW phone the user signs in again (the Navidrome password could never be decrypted there anyway).

controls.title: Clipboard and sensitive screen exposure
controls.evidence: The clipboard receives only public links (music.youtube.com/watch, party invite without token) and diagnostics that pass DiagnosticText.clean + OnlineDiagnostics.redact. Password fields are masked. FLAG_SECURE is not used: no secret is ever displayed.

controls.title: Native libraries and dynamically loaded code
controls.evidence: Native python/ffmpeg come from youtubedl-android inside the signed APK. yt-dlp (Python code) self-updates from GitHub releases (youtubedl-android YoutubeDLUpdater) over HTTPS with system CAs, but without signature verification. Plain HTTP to github.com/githubusercontent.com is now impossible (network security config).
controls.remediation: Accepted risk unless you decide otherwise: verifying yt-dlp's GPG signature in-app is a larger change; turning auto-update off would break downloads as YouTube changes.

controls.title: ProGuard / R8 release hardening
controls.evidence: R8 is off on purpose (reflection-heavy NewPipe/Rhino/yt-dlp code). MImic is open source (public GPL repository), so obfuscation would hide nothing; it is not a security control for this app.

controls.title: User-controlled input and content URIs
controls.evidence: Server and party URLs are normalised (http/https only, no query/fragment); invite and shared links are parsed defensively; content URIs come only from the app's own FileProviders with per-URI read grants; new tests cover hostile links.

controls.title: Android Keystore encryption
controls.evidence: CredentialCipher: AES-256-GCM, non-exportable Android Keystore key, random IV, failure-tolerant. YouTube session: EncryptedSharedPreferences (Keystore-wrapped AES-256-SIV/GCM) that repairs a stale keyset.

controls.title: Navidrome credentials protected at rest
controls.evidence: Only ciphertext is stored (password_enc); a legacy plaintext password is migrated on first run; plaintext is written only if the Keystore is unusable (rare OEM fallback, documented). Now excluded from backups.

controls.title: Credentials kept out of logs and analytics
controls.evidence: No analytics or crash SDK. Every Log.* call reviewed: no passwords, tokens, cookies or stream URLs. Diagnostic exports are redacted (OnlineDiagnostics.redact, DiagnosticText.clean; unit-tested).

controls.title: Token and session handling
controls.evidence: Subsonic salted-token auth (t = md5(password+salt), fresh salt per request); the password itself is never sent. Party token in app-private prefs, never logged, now excluded from backup. YouTube cookies encrypted; sign-out clears them.
controls.remediation: On a plain-HTTP network a sniffer could replay a t/s pair: use HTTPS (Tailscale Serve) for remote access.

controls.title: TLS certificate and hostname validation
controls.evidence: No custom TrustManager, HostnameVerifier, sslSocketFactory or onReceivedSslError anywhere. The network security config trusts system CAs only (user-installed CAs cannot intercept).

controls.title: HTTP exceptions and network security configuration
controls.evidence: Before: usesCleartextTraffic=true for everything. Now: network_security_config.xml keeps HTTP for home Navidrome servers and HTTP radio streams (required), but makes github.com, api.github.com, *.githubusercontent.com, *.googleapis.com, accounts.google.com, music/www.youtube.com and lrclib.net HTTPS-only. Lint's InsecureBaseConfiguration warning is acknowledged (by design).

controls.title: Credentials in background services and notifications
controls.evidence: Notifications show song titles and progress only; WorkManager inputs carry video ids, never tokens; Cast uses a LAN server with random 128-bit per-song tokens so the Navidrome token never reaches the TV.

controls.title: Disconnect, logout and credential clearing
controls.evidence: Full sign-out clears the whole server store; 'Switch account' removes user and password but keeps the address; YouTube Music sign-out clears Google cookies; leaving a party removes its token.

controls.title: Remote download URLs and redirect destinations
controls.evidence: Updater: HTTPS + GitHub host allowlist enforced on every redirect hop (network interceptor). Navidrome downloads go only to the configured server. Media links (yt-dlp) are user-initiated by design.

controls.title: Path traversal and unsafe filenames
controls.evidence: Navidrome download names: only [A-Za-z0-9._-], never '.', '..' or hidden, at most 120 characters (new DownloadRepository.safeFileName + tests; ordinary ids unchanged). Online downloads: yt_<videoId> restricted the same way. Downloader titles: FileNaming.sanitize (unit-tested).

controls.title: Download size, content type and integrity
controls.evidence: Updater: new size cap (the release-stated size, at most 400 MB), ZIP magic check, SHA-256 against SHA256SUMS.txt, parseable APK. Media downloads are user-initiated and parsed by Media3/tagging (no size cap; a bad file just fails to play).

controls.title: Temporary files and offline caches
controls.evidence: All in app-private storage (filesDir/cacheDir); .part files deleted on failure or cancel; update files cleaned at start-up; sharing only through FileProviders limited to specific folders.

controls.title: Media metadata and artwork parsing
controls.evidence: Parsing by Android/Media3/Coil decoders; metadata shown as plain Compose text (no HTML rendering); malformed server JSON handled by tested fail-safe parsers. Not fuzzed.

controls.title: GitHub release download integrity
controls.evidence: HTTPS + host allowlist; SHA256SUMS.txt is treated as a corruption check only (same source as the APK); authenticity comes from the pinned signing certificate. The release script re-downloads and verifies every published asset.

controls.title: APK signing identity verified before installation
controls.evidence: The APK must be signed by exactly the pinned certificate C03C5107...087D AND match the installed app's signer; the checks now live in UpdateVerification and are covered by unit tests (wrong key, extra signer, no signer, malformed pin, installed-key mismatch).

controls.title: Update downgrade and package-substitution attacks
controls.evidence: Package must equal com.example.mimic and versionCode must be strictly higher (equal = reinstall, refused); the release name's versionCode is also compared before download. Unit-tested. Android's installer always asks the user.

controls.title: Navidrome/Subsonic authentication and server responses
controls.evidence: Salted-token auth; responses parsed defensively (status checks, null-safe JSON); clients have connect/read timeouts; certificate validation is the system's.

controls.title: YouTube and other online integrations
controls.evidence: HTTPS-only (now enforced for youtube/googleapis); session encrypted; PoToken WebView offline; resolver logs redacted before export; YouTube region never spoofed.

controls.title: Vulnerable and outdated dependencies
controls.evidence: OSV scan of 345 resolved release dependencies: 32 advisories found. 9 fixed by raising jsoup to 1.23.2, Guava to 33.7.2-android, protobuf-javalite to 3.25.8 and Jackson from 2.11.1 to 2.13.5. 23 remain, all inside youtubedl-android (full edition): commons-compress 1.12, commons-io 2.5, Jackson 2.13.5. Reviewed as not reachable (bundled archives only; no polymorphic typing, async parser, etc.) and listed with reasons in scripts/security/osv-allowlist.txt; the gate blocks any new unreviewed HIGH/CRITICAL.
controls.remediation: Owner decision: the remaining fixes need Android 8+ (minSdk 26) or replacing youtubedl-android.

controls.title: GitHub Actions and release permissions
controls.evidence: All actions pinned to reviewed commit SHAs (Dependabot proposes updates), read-only token, persist-credentials false, Gradle wrapper validation, security checks separate from publishing; publishing is local with the maintainer's key only. Branch protection on main blocks force-push and deletion.

controls.title: Privacy-safe error reporting and suspicious-event diagnostics
controls.evidence: No telemetry by design. Download Diagnostics and Online diagnostics are local and redacted; rejected updates (untrusted host, checksum, signature, downgrade) are shown to the user by name and logged with public values only.

controls.title: Automated security regression tests
controls.evidence: New SecurityRegressionTest (14 tests, both editions), manifest checker, Gitleaks/OSV gate in scripts/release.sh, GitHub workflows security.yml (PR/main/weekly) and codeql.yml.
